summary: Webhook callbacks failing SSL/TLS validation (certificate chain / hostname verification errors)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports Redwood webhook delivery failures to their callback endpoint with SSL/TLS validation errors.
- Failures began after customer-side infrastructure changes (new load balancer / certificate rotation) per customer report.

Customer impact
- Webhook events (job completion + alert notifications) not being delivered consistently.
- Customer is missing downstream automation triggers; manual reconciliation required.

Customer environment
- Tier: Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- Callback URL (redacted): https://<customer-domain>/redwood/webhooks
- Customer notes: traffic terminates at a managed LB/CDN layer; origin is internal.

What we see (Redwood side)
- Redwood delivery attempts failing during TLS handshake / certificate validation.
- Error variants observed in delivery logs:
  - "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"
  - "x509: certificate is not valid for any names, but wanted to match <customer-domain>"
  - "remote error: tls: handshake failure" (intermittent)
- Retries continue per webhook retry policy; no indication of Redwood-side outage.

Request IDs / evidence
- Example delivery attempt IDs (internal): wh_deliv_7c2d9f1a, wh_deliv_7c2da41e
- Sample timestamps (UTC): 2026-02-13 16:42–17:10

Support-safe troubleshooting checklist (customer-facing)
1) Confirm the callback URL and hostname
   - Ensure the hostname in the webhook URL exactly matches the certificate CN/SAN (including subdomain).
   - If the endpoint recently changed (new LB / new subdomain), update the webhook configuration to match.

2) Verify the certificate is publicly trusted
   - Redwood webhook delivery validates certificates against standard public trust stores.
   - Self-signed certificates and private/internal CAs are not supported for webhook callbacks.
   - Cloud/CDN “origin certificates” that are not publicly trusted can cause "unknown authority" failures.

3) Ensure the server presents the full certificate chain (leaf + intermediate)
   - Common failure: server only returns the leaf cert and omits the intermediate.
   - Ask the customer to verify using:
     - openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <host> -showcerts
   - Confirm the output includes the intermediate certificate(s) needed to build a chain to a trusted root.

4) Check TLS policy compatibility
   - Ensure TLS 1.2+ is enabled.
   - Avoid requiring mTLS (client certificates). Redwood webhooks do not present a client certificate.
   - Ensure SNI is enabled/handled correctly on the LB (server should select the cert for the requested hostname).

5) Confirm there is no redirect or HTTP-to-HTTPS loop
   - Redwood follows standard redirects conservatively; redirects to a different hostname can fail hostname validation.
   - Ensure the callback returns 2xx within the expected timeout window.

6) If using a CDN/WAF
   - Ensure the CDN/WAF is configured to accept requests from Redwood and is not downgrading or re-terminating TLS incorrectly.
   - If the CDN uses an origin cert, ensure the edge cert (public-facing) is what Redwood connects to.

What Support needs from the customer (if still failing)
- Output of: openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <host> -showcerts (with any private keys removed)
- Confirmation of TLS versions enabled and whether mTLS is required
- Whether the endpoint is behind Cloudflare/Akamai/ALB/NLB (provider + mode)
- A timestamp window of failures and the current callback URL

Internal notes / escalation guidance
- If errors indicate chain/hostname issues, do not escalate to SRE until customer confirms a valid publicly trusted cert and complete chain.
- Escalate to Platform (Control Plane) if we suspect webhook configuration mismatch, redirect behavior, or if delivery attempt logs contradict customer reports.
- If multiple customers report similar TLS failures across regions within a short time window, move to #incidents and page SRE per escalation playbook.

Current ask
- Validate whether the customer’s endpoint is presenting a complete chain and a certificate valid for the configured hostname.
- Provide customer with the checklist above and request openssl output.

resolution: Resolved after customer corrected TLS termination and certificate presentation. Root cause was customer endpoint presenting an untrusted/incorrect certificate (Cloudflare origin-style / private trust) and incomplete chain (missing intermediate), leading to Redwood webhook TLS verification failures. After switching to a publicly trusted certificate for the external hostname and serving the full chain, webhook deliveries succeeded.
